name: mitigation mechanism
definition: Harris's three-way distinction (2023): allocation assigns the risk to a named party by contract; spreading transfers it to third parties for a premium; pooling mutualises it among stakeholders with no outsider. The sort key of this census, and the characteristic on which Harris's own open question turns - under which conditions was risk spread as opposed to pooled or allocated.

name: membership basis
definition: Ground on which a participant belongs to the pool.

name: entry restriction
definition: Membership is closed or numerically restricted (1 = restricted).

name: participation basis
definition: Whether participation is chosen or imposed. Theoretically loaded: if pooling raises each participant's time-average growth rate, compulsion demands an explanation, and the non-excludability of the pooled good is the usual one.

name: contribution timing
definition: When contributions fall due. ex-post-assessment is the general-average pattern (contribute after the loss); ex-ante is the fund pattern.

name: contribution basis
definition: How each member's contribution is measured.

name: contribution enforceability
definition: Non-payment can be compelled or sanctioned (1 = enforceable).

name: hazard correlation
definition: Correlation of the hazard across members, which sets the sign of the pooling. Idiosyncratic hazards diversify; covariate hazards synchronise and can make the pool worse than no pool.

name: hazard responsiveness
definition: The hazard responds to the defence mounted against it (1 = adversarial, e.g. an enemy fleet; 0 = indifferent, e.g. a storm).

name: pool output
definition: What the pool actually produces. collective-good: the fund buys something non-excludable for all members (convoy escort, city walls) and no individual draws on it. individual-indemnity: a member is compensated for a realised loss. individual-draw: a member receives the pot by rotation, lot or auction irrespective of loss. PY1-PY3 presuppose an individual payout and are inapplicable where PY0 is collective-good - a distinction the first coded form (averia_pool) forced, since PY1 as originally written silently assumed distribution.

name: payout trigger
definition: What entitles a member to draw on the pool.

name: allocation rule
definition: How the draw is allocated among eligible members. Meaningful only where PY1 does not already determine it.

name: payout cap
definition: The draw is capped independently of the loss suffered (1 = capped).

name: loss-sharing rule
definition: How an unmet loss is distributed once the pool is exhausted or insufficient.

name: residual claim on fund
definition: Members hold a claim on the fund's surplus (1 = yes).

name: liability beyond contribution
definition: A member can be pursued beyond what he has contributed or agreed to contribute (1 = exposed, 0 = shielded). The participant-side barrier question, and the direct analogue of AP3 in organizational_forms.

name: loss verification mode
definition: HOW a claimed loss is established — the MODE ONLY. Split from the object of verification on 2026-08-13; before that this characteristic silently asked two questions and the values below answer only the first. See VF2 for WHAT is established. The split rests on discriminant-validity evidence in Campbell & Fiske's sense: across five forms one mode takes three objects and one object takes three modes, and in friendly_society_england a communal mode carries a dual object within a single form. Bears on whether the coupling can operate at all; candidate for promotion to outcome-coupling once forms separate it from PY1.

name: verification object
definition: WHAT is established before payment, as distinct from how. loss-occurrence: that the defined misfortune happened or persists. claimant-need: that the claimant has been reduced to want, irrespective of the event. claimant-fault: that the misfortune did not arise from the claimant's own misconduct. conduct-compliance: that the claimant is observing the conditions of relief while drawing it. mixed: two or more of these at once. Ontologically dependent on VF1 — an object of verification presupposes that verification occurs — so VF2 is .NA wherever VF1 is 'none'. Added 2026-08-13 as the repair of a conflation, not as added resolution: the motivating evidence is in the VF1 notes of guild_box_brabant, guild_box_dutch, guild_relief_england, craft_pension_edinburgh and friendly_society_england, and in logbook 4.

name: governance mode
definition: Locus of decision-making over the fund.

name: pool duration
definition: Intended life of the arrangement. A rotating association completes a cycle; a levy runs indefinitely.

name: terminal distribution
definition: What happens to the fund at dissolution. Meaningful only where DR1 is not open-ended.

name: peril-risk bearer
definition: Who bears loss from the peril itself - shipwreck, seizure, jettison. Harris's key observation on the sea loan is that peril risk and market risk were allocated to DIFFERENT parties, which RB1/RB2 record separately.

name: market-risk bearer
definition: Who bears loss from price movement and failed sale. In the sea loan the borrower keeps this while the lender takes the peril risk; in the commenda both are shared.

name: security or pledge
definition: What secures the advance. THE CELL THAT SEPARATES BOTTOMRY FROM RESPONDENTIA: bottomry is secured on the ship, respondentia on the goods (Harris 2023). Both are medieval refinements of the generic sea loan. VALUE SET WIDENED 2026-08-09 on the tanomoshi-ko evidence, which the original maritime set could not hold: 'cargo' renamed 'goods' so that movables in trade take one state whether at sea or in a warehouse (the at-peril question is RB4's, not this one); 'real-estate' added for land, town lots and storehouses; 'surety' split out of 'personal', which was doing duty both for security on the borrower's own estate and for a third party standing behind him - Kato 1998, 147 makes the suretyship mandatory BECAUSE foreclosure was slow in some jurisdictions, so the two are distinct facts; 'mixed' for arrangements taking property and surety together. Does NOT cover a member pledging his claim ON a pool to secure borrowing OUTSIDE it (Matsunaga 1999, 297) - that is a second question and belongs to transferable claims in organizational_forms.

name: discharge on total loss
definition: The obligation is extinguished if the venture is lost (1 = discharged). The sea loan's defining feature and the reason canon law read it as usurious: the lender is paid for bearing peril.

name: peril priced ex ante
definition: Whether the cost of bearing the peril is set before the event (1 = priced). Deliberately says PERIL, not risk: the characteristic measures the movement from a hazard conception (an event that may befall, no distribution, not priceable) to a risk conception (a quantified distribution, priceable, transferable to a party with no stake), so it cannot be named with the endpoint of the shift it measures. Knight's threshold as Harris applies it: general average needs no ex-ante price because all calculation is ex post, which is why it is ancient; premium insurance requires one, which is why it waits until c.1300; the sea loan prices crudely and sits between.
